assets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: photographic pond-water background texture for a microscope game. Transform the supplied real microscope photograph into a new WIDE 3:2 field of view with the exact same ordinary transmitted-light / phase-contrast optical character: cloudy warm gray water, fine dirty sediment, tiny refracting rods, tiny near-transparent vesicles, weak olive pigments, subtle purple/cyan/gold chromatic fringes, varied defocus and imperfect focus. Zoom the apparent magnification OUT substantially: ALL rods, fragments and biological details must be TINY, none wider than 2 percent of the canvas. Remove the two huge prominent diatoms and the large black sediment clumps. Replace them with scattered much smaller irregular debris. An uneven natural distribution, quiet areas between tiny colonies, lower density near the center, no composed hero subject. A photograph taken through a real low-cost microscope eyepiece, NOT a 3D render: no embossed glass sculpture, no decorative amoeba icons, no luminous CGI membranes, no underwater beams, no neon, no sparkling fantasy scene. Soft diffuse nearly flat transmitted illumination across the whole frame, pale neutral gray with faint khaki tint, restrained microcontrast; slight optical softness, fine sensor texture, authentic transparent specimens with paired light-and-dark refractive edges. Nothing sharp and larger than a dust-sized fleck; no strong dark clumps. Seamless-looking continuous water field to all four edges, no vignette or microscope circular frame, no text, labels, UI, grids, arrows, watermarks. Landscape photographic material plate, about 1536 by 1024 or larger. This is a NEW sibling background based on the reference, not an edit to the source file.

assets.status: Used as a 2x2 transparent atlas for 29 independently drifting specimens
assets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a transparent 2 by 2 sprite atlas of FOUR different tiny pond-water specimens, derived from the ordinary real microscope optical look in the attached photograph. The input is the optical/material reference, not content to paste. Square atlas, four equal square quadrants with generous transparent padding, each contains ONE complete different specimen centered entirely inside its quadrant. TOP LEFT: a very slender horizontal pointed pennate diatom with two irregular dull olive-brown chloroplasts, delicate dark and bright refractive paired shell edges, faint silica ribs, exactly the photographic character of the reference's largest diatom. TOP RIGHT: a small irregular oval transparent protozoan with hazy cytoplasm, a few pale gray vacuoles, weak dark-gray outline, not a shining glass cell. BOTTOM LEFT: a small round to slightly oval empty transparent diatom shell, faint charcoal phase halo, one subtle amber-brown pigment granule and imperfect fine internal speckling. BOTTOM RIGHT: a loose irregular crumb of organic detritus, a small aggregate of tiny brown-gray grains and transparent fragments with softly blurred edges, no round cell silhouette. All four rendered like photographs through a real transmitted-light phase-contrast microscope, imperfect focus, paired subtle light/dark edge halos and very restrained purple/cyan/gold fringe, predominantly neutral gray transparency and dull olive pigment. NO glossy 3D render, NO science-fiction cells, NO blue or icy material, NO glowing membrane, NO white cilia fringe, NO dramatic volumetric lighting, NO fantasy amoeba icons, NO solid gray rectangular panels. Their bodies should retain real semi-transparent alpha as appropriate and their outside must be genuine alpha transparency. Each single specimen occupies at most 72 percent width and 60 percent height of its own quadrant; nothing touches another quadrant, no objects at outer borders. No text, labels, grid lines, numbers, background, shadows outside specimens, UI, watermark. They will be rendered at 20 to 40 pixels wide over a gray microscope plate. Preserve the reference's subtle dirty real-world character over decorative beauty. New sibling art asset; never alter the reference file.
